evidence.quote: When using `--maxfail` and the max fails is reached in a certain worker
the worker executes session fixture teardown twice.

proposal.framework: pytest subprocess integration test using pytester with pytest-xdist
proposal.setup: Build a local suite with one deliberate assertion failure and enough passing cases to involve two workers. Use an autouse session fixture with setup and teardown markers in separate per-worker files under a temporary directory.
steps: Run the synthetic suite under pytest-xdist with two workers and --maxfail=1. Use bounded worker coordination to ensure both workers have entered the fixture before the deliberate failure.
Confirm the run reached the deliberate failure. Read setup and teardown counts for every worker that entered the fixture.
Run the same suite without --maxfail as a control. Compare the proposed check on pinned affected and corrected pytest revisions with the same xdist version.
proposal.assertion: The subprocess reports the deliberate test failure, both workers record fixture setup, and each participating worker records exactly one corresponding teardown.
proposal.predicted_failure: The affected --maxfail path records duplicate teardown for a worker. Worker startup errors, missing markers, unrelated exceptions, and coordination timeouts are incomplete runs.
proposal.rationale: Inferred: each worker should finalize its session fixture once after the failure limit stops the run. Confirm the assertion and the activation conditions against the upstream fix and the no-limit control.

upstream_execution.reason: Only the proposal and its source quotations were validated.

limitations: Worker scheduling and dependency versions can affect reproducibility. Coordination and revision selection are still proposed.
The linked xdist issue reports duplicate fixture execution, while the primary pytest issue describes duplicate teardown. The proposed assertion targets the primary issue.
